Lemma
[the geodesic field]

↗ def:dc-ch3-2-1

1. ch3:2.3

There exists a unique vector field $G$ on $TM$ whose trajectories are of the form $t\mapsto (\gamma (t),\gamma '(t))$, where $\gamma $ is a geodesic on $M$.
Proof

\sketch Uniqueness: in a coordinate system $(U,\mathbf{x})$ the trajectories of $G$ on $TU$ are $t\mapsto (\gamma (t),\gamma '(t))$ with $\gamma $ a geodesic, hence solutions of (1’); by uniqueness of trajectories of such a system, $G$ is unique if it exists. Existence: define $G$ locally by (1’); uniqueness shows $G$ is well-defined on all of $TM$.

□
